overview: The Medford Human Rights Commission recapped a recent public event, elected a new secretary, and issued a formal statement regarding a fatal police shooting in Cambridge. The commission also formed subcommittees to begin reviewing structural recommendations and ordinance revisions proposed by Safe Medford.

items.title: Introductions and International Women's Day Recognition
items.summary: Commissioners and community guests introduced themselves and acknowledged International Women's Day.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The commission approved the minutes from the previous meeting.

items.title: Belinda Sutton Event Recap
items.summary: The commission discussed the success of the recent Belinda Sutton petition reading event at the Royall House and Slave Quarters, which featured performances by the Tufts S-Fact group.

items.title: Election of Secretary
items.summary: The commission elected Diane McDonald as Secretary and discussed the need to formalize the role's responsibilities and public relations duties.

items.title: Statement on the Death of Sayed Faisal
items.summary: The commission approved a statement expressing condolences for Sayed Faisal and calling for increased investment in mental health resources and unarmed crisis response teams.

items.title: Safe Medford Proposal and Ordinance Review
items.summary: Members deliberated on operational recommendations from Safe Medford regarding the commission's authority to handle discrimination complaints and the necessity of updating the city ordinance.

items.title: Formation of Subcommittees and Assignments
items.summary: The commission established three subcommittees to review the city ordinance, develop recruitment materials, and condense operational goals for future implementation.
